name: Bakatue

card.when: The first Tuesday of July, with a durbar that Saturday
card.sum: Elmina opens the Benya lagoon: the chief casts a net three times, then come the regatta and a durbar at the castle.

metaTitle: Bakatue: Opening of the Benya Lagoon in Elmina
metaDescription: Bakatue, “the opening of the lagoon”, is Elmina’s July festival: six sacred weeks end with the chief casting a net into the Benya lagoon, a regatta and a durbar at the castle.
subtitle: Elmina opens its lagoon
answer: Bakatue, Fante for “the opening of the lagoon”, is the July festival of Elmina in the Central Region. After six sacred weeks with fishing banned in the Benya lagoon, the paramount chief casts a ceremonial net into the water three times on the first Tuesday of July, the ban is lifted, and there is a regatta. A grand durbar at Elmina Castle follows on the Saturday.

sticky.title: First Tuesday of July
sticky.text: Be at the Benya lagoon for the net casting, then come back on Saturday for the durbar.

sections.title: The sacred weeks and the opening

days.label: Early June
days.title: Six sacred weeks begin
days.html: Fishing in the lagoon and noise-making are banned. Fresh farm produce may not be sold in Elmina and fish only at the landing beaches; the bereaved may not wail, and anyone who dies is buried the same day.[[2]]

days.label: Three weeks before
days.title: A fast for the gods
days.html: A holy wooden platter is turned over to begin a three-week fast for the gods, and priests and priestesses hold sacred drumming and dancing, the Dombo ceremonies.[[2]]

days.label: First Tuesday of July
days.title: The net is cast
days.html: Chiefs, queen mothers and priests process from the palace to the lagoon. The Edinamanhen offers mashed yam, herbs and eggs to break the gods’ fast, then casts his net three times; each cast brings in fish, and the last is met with gunfire, music and dance.[[2]] The ban is lifted and a regatta follows, with women’s groups out on the water in canoes.[[1,2]]

days.label: Saturday
days.title: The durbar
days.html: The festival closes with a grand durbar on the forecourt of Elmina Castle.[[2]]

sections.title: What Bakatue remembers
sections.html: Bakatue marks the founding of Elmina. One telling has the founder, Kwa Amankwa, finding water at the stream he named Be-enya, and meeting a deity there who stayed for eight days; the festival honours that meeting.[[3]]

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: the Benya lagoon runs behind Elmina Castle; the net casting is on its banks.
Two days to see: the Tuesday for the rites and regatta, the Saturday for the durbar.
During the sacred weeks: respect the bans in town, especially on noise.
Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.
In January: Elmina also keeps Edina Bronya.

faq.a: It is Fante for “the opening of the lagoon”, the Benya lagoon at Elmina.
On the first Tuesday of July, after six sacred weeks, with a grand durbar at Elmina Castle that Saturday.
The paramount chief casts a ceremonial net into the lagoon three times to lift the fishing ban, followed by a regatta and a durbar.
